name: Escher Foyer
description: M.C. Escher 'Relativity' (1953) inspired stone architecture tileset. Pen-and-ink crosshatch rendering, multiple implied gravity planes. 512x512 source images designed for downscaling to 32x32 in-engine.

edge_types.FLAT: Stone surface flush with tile edge — connects to any other FLAT edge
edge_types.VOID: Open air — connects to any other VOID edge
edge_types.STEP: Stair tread nosing meeting the tile edge mid-pixel

tiles.description: Pure open air. Faint atmospheric grain lines at 7° off-horizontal. No structure. Tiles in any direction without seams.
Full solid stone slab. All edges FLAT — stacks in any direction to form larger stone masses.
Walkable floor surface: 96px slab at top, void below. Tiles horizontally to form continuous floor runs.
Floor slab with left drop-off. Slab occupies right 416px; left 96px void. Exposed left vertical face rendered.
Floor slab with right drop-off. Mirror of floor_surface_left_edge.
Overhead ceiling surface. 96px slab at bottom, void above. Underside lit — readable as floor under inverted gravity. Complement to floor_surface for Relativity double-gravity corridors.
Vertical stone wall occupying left 96px. Exposed right face rendered. Stacks vertically for full-height walls.
Mirror of wall_left_face. Wall occupies right 96px, exposed left face.
Single step ascending left-to-right. Tread right half, riser center. Tile horizontally for continuous ascending staircase. Combine with stair_turn_ne / stair_turn_sw as bookends.
Single step ascending right-to-left. Mirror of stair_ascending_right. Tile horizontally for continuous left-ascending staircase. Combine with stair_turn_nw / stair_turn_se as bookends.
Two steps per tile, ascending left-to-right. Use when staircase must rise steeply in fewer tiles.

Horizontal stone landing with flag-joint seam detail. All edges FLAT — universal adjacency. Gravity-reversal junction: a landing from which staircases depart in opposite directions reads as floor or ceiling depending on which staircase you follow.
L-corner: staircase arriving from west, wall rising north. Lower floor strip + right wall strip. Connects stair_ascending_right (left) with wall_left_face (above).
L-corner: staircase arriving from east, wall rising north. Mirror of stair_turn_ne.
L-corner: staircase descending to ground level, east corridor. Terminates ascending staircase at floor on right side.
L-corner: staircase descending to ground level, west corridor. Mirror of stair_turn_se.
Ionic column capital (top). Volute scrolls at upper corners. Flares from 128px shaft to 192px capital. Stack above pillar_shaft tiles; place below floor_slab or ceiling.
Cylindrical column shaft segment. 128px wide, full height. Drum joint every 128px. Stack as many as needed between pillar_cap_top and pillar_cap_bottom.
Column base capital. 180° rotation of pillar_cap_top. Functions as conventional base under normal gravity OR as capital under inverted gravity — enabling Escher ambiguity.
Left springing stone of a semicircular arch. Quarter-circle intrados from bottom-right corner to top. Arch center implied at tile bottom-right corner. Place left of arch_keystone.
Arch crown keystone. Slightly projecting voussoir. Arch center at tile bottom-center. Place between arch_left_springer and arch_right_springer to complete the semicircle.
Right springing stone of a semicircular arch. Mirror of arch_left_springer. Arch center at tile bottom-left corner.

Signature Relativity junction tile. Two stone slabs (top 96px and bottom 96px) with 320px void between, connected by wall strips on both sides forming a tunnel cross-section. Contradictory shadow directions make the tile readable as floor from one gravity and ceiling from another simultaneously.
Full wall tile with centered semicircular arched window opening. All four edges FLAT — drops into any wall run. The void interior suggests depth and inhabitation.

Gravity-shift corner: east-system floor meets west-system wall. L-mass in lower-right quadrant. Equal-density hatching at the 90° corner creates visual ambiguity about which surface is floor and which is wall. Use at the junction between a staircase run and a corridor on a perpendicular gravity plane.
Mirror of transition_gravity_west. L-mass in lower-left quadrant. Place as a pair with transition_gravity_west flanking a floor run to produce the three-gravity-system reading of Relativity.

staircase_loop.description: Closed Escher loop — ascending right along bottom, ascending left along top, connected by landings. Reads as infinite staircase from either gravity.

relativity_corridor.description: 3x3 arrangement creating double-gravity corridor readable from two directions
